name: Pipe Organ
shortDescription: Pressurised-air instrument producing continuous tones through vibrating air columns in pipes controlled by keyboard manuals.
description: The pipe organ is the largest and most complex musical instrument. Pressurised air from bellows or an electric blower feeds a wind chest. When a key is depressed, a pallet opens admitting air into one or more organ pipes. Edge tones or reed tongues set the air column into resonance, producing a continuous, non-decaying tone for as long as the key is held.
historicalOrigins: The hydraulis (water organ) was invented by Ctesibius of Alexandria around 246 BCE. The medieval portative organ evolved into the great cathedral pipe organ by the 15th century.
acousticPrinciples: Edge tones: air jet striking a sharp edge (flue pipes) creates vortex oscillation coupling to pipe resonant length
Reed pipes: metal tongue vibrates against shallot at natural frequency, exciting air column
Pipe length sets fundamental pitch: open pipe = λ/2, stopped pipe = λ/4 (one octave lower)
Stops (registers) engage/disengage pipe ranks, combining timbres additively

characteristics.pitchRange: C0 (16.4 Hz) to C8 (4186 Hz) depending on ranks
characteristics.dynamicRange: Fixed per stop; 50–110 dB by stop selection
characteristics.timbralColor: Limitless via stop combinations: pure flute, bright principal, buzzy reed
characteristics.orchestralRole: Liturgical accompaniment, choral foundation, solo virtuosity

soundDNA.exciter: Air jet striking a lip (flue) or vibrating metal tongue (reed) in each pipe
soundDNA.resonator: Metal or wooden cylindrical/conical pipe cavity of specific length
soundDNA.harmonics: Stop-dependent: open flute = fundamental only; Mixture = high harmonics added
soundDNA.attackDecay: Virtually instant onset when key opens; sustained indefinitely; stops instantly at key release
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Pure and regal; highly variable by stop selection from soft flute to full plenum
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Pipes radiate outward from pipe mouth; large instruments fill reverberant cathedral space

pipes.label: Pipe Ranks
pipes.function: Rows of cylindrical or conical pipes, each producing one pitch. Open pipes = half-wavelength resonance.

characteristics.material: Lead/tin alloy (metal pipes) or wood (wooden pipes)
characteristics.mechanism: Air column resonance at λ/2 (open) or λ/4 (stopped)
characteristics.role: Primary tone generator for each pitch

manuals.label: Keyboard Manuals
manuals.function: One or more 61-key manuals (keyboards) connecting key to pallet valves for each pipe rank.

characteristics.material: Ivory or phenolic key surfaces, wooden key levers
characteristics.mechanism: Mechanical or electric key action opens wind-chest pallet

stops.label: Stop Knobs / Drawbars
stops.function: Registers activating specific pipe ranks. Combining stops creates additive timbral mixtures.

characteristics.mechanism: Slider gate admitting wind to selected pipe rank

wind_chest.label: Wind Chest
wind_chest.function: Pressurised air manifold beneath pipes. Pallets open to admit air to individual pipes.

characteristics.material: Sealed wooden chest with leather pallet valves

bellows.label: Blower & Bellows
bellows.function: Electric blower or foot-pumped bellows maintains constant regulated air pressure (typical: 75–100mm WC).

characteristics.material: Electric centrifugal blower or leather-covered bellows

pedal_board.label: Pedal Board
pedal_board.function: 32-note concave/radiating pedalboard played by organist's feet, controlling the lowest bass pipes.

characteristics.material: Wooden pedals in AGO/BDO standard layout
characteristics.mechanism: Same key-action as manuals for bass pipe ranks

followTheSound.title: Pressurised Air Supply
followTheSound.explanation: Electric blower maintains constant wind pressure feeding the wind chest.

followTheSound.title: Pallet Opens
followTheSound.explanation: Depressing a key opens a pallet valve, admitting pressurised air to the pipe.

followTheSound.title: Pipe Resonance
followTheSound.explanation: Air jet strikes pipe mouth edge (flue) or reed tongue, exciting the pipe air column into resonance.

followTheSound.title: Stop Mixture
followTheSound.explanation: Active stops determine which pipe ranks sound simultaneously, creating additive timbral combinations.
